caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
raw_response: This bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, comparing six different multilingual BERT model configurations – mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2 – across nine language families. The horizontal axis represents the language families, ordered alphabetically as IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis represents the “effect” value, ranging from approximately 0 to 30, with a linear scale and tick intervals of 5. The bars are colored differently to represent each model configuration: mBERT-L2 is depicted in light blue, XLM-L2 in dark blue, mBERT-R2 in orange, XLM-R2 in dark orange, mBERT-B2 in red, and XLM-B2 in purple. The bars are accompanied by error bars, representing standard deviation, which vary in length across the different language families and model configurations. The bar for IE-Indic is the tallest, reaching approximately 25, while the bars for Isolate and Uralic families are consistently the shortest, reaching approximately 1. The IE-Germanic family consistently exhibits higher effect values than the IE-Romance family, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars, indicating the highest variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. Within the IE-Slavic family, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) consistently show larger effect values than the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large as those of the L2 and R2 variants.
